# Plan: Team Notes

## Approach

This plan confirms the declared artifact layout exactly as listed in the specification; no path is added, renamed, or dropped. Work that would normally live in a separate file (TLS setup, error handling, the backup job, the mail transport, the ownership helper, the shared note-content writer, the confirmation dialog helper) is placed in the declared file named by the task that introduces it. Build output under dist/ comes from a package.json script and is not a source artifact.

Stack: Node.js 22 LTS and TypeScript executed through tsx, so no tsconfig.json is required. The server is Express on node:https with better-sqlite3 (SQLite with FTS5). The schema in src/server/db/schema.sql is applied at startup. Every user-owned row has a random UUID text primary key, so a deleted item's identifier is never reused. The client is plain TypeScript modules plus a TipTap (ProseMirror) editor, bundled by esbuild from a package.json script. Tests run on the built-in node:test runner through tsx, after a pretest step builds the client bundle. API tests start an in-process HTTPS server from the createApp() factory exported by src/server/app.ts, using a certificate generated by selfsigned. Browser tests drive the playwright library programmatically, looping over the OD-024 browser projects and over desktop and mobile viewports. Accessibility scans use @axe-core/playwright, and PDF text is extracted in tests with pdfjs-dist. This setup needs no configuration files outside the approved scope. Test fixtures such as images, PDFs, and documents are generated as bytes inside the test files.

Note text is stored exactly as typed, with no Unicode normalization. Only lookup keys (normalized email and tag name_key) are normalized.

Note list semantics: the list endpoint takes a scope of active (not archived and not trashed; the default for the dashboard and folder views), archived, or any (active and archived, never trashed). The Pinned, Open tasks, and tag destinations use scope any and mark archived notes with an Archived badge, so each lists exactly the matching notes. Under the default sort, the dashboard and folder views show a Pinned section first and then the unpinned notes ordered by last update, newest first. The pinned sort lists pinned notes first and then orders by last update. Every other sort shows one list ordered strictly by its field.

## Open decision defaults

Each default below is a named constant or environment variable, so resolving an open decision changes a value and not the structure. OD-001, OD-002, and OD-004 are high severity, and the operator must confirm them before delivery is accepted.

- OD-001: trash retention is 30 days, set per deployment through TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS. There is no per-user setting in this release.
- OD-002: the attachment size limit is 25 MB through ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES. The limit appears in the upload control's help text and in the rejection message.
- OD-003: supported images are PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP, and all four get inline previews. Supported documents are DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, and RTF, plus PDF and plain text. The type is checked by both extension and sniffed magic bytes.
- OD-004: a save first snapshots the previous content as a version if any of these holds: no version exists yet and the previous body is non-empty; 5 minutes have passed since the last version; or at least 50 percent of the previous body text changed, measured by common-prefix and common-suffix difference. Replacing the entire body always qualifies.
- OD-005: the newest 100 versions per note are kept. Pruning runs only when an auto-save creates a version, never during a restore.
- OD-006: auto-save fires 1000 ms after typing stops.
- OD-007 and OD-008: these are performance targets with no acceptance criterion. Search uses indexed FTS5 queries; there is no measurement harness in this release.
- OD-009: results are ranked by bm25 relevance, with the most recent updated_at breaking ties.
- OD-010: matches are highlighted with mark elements in the title and body snippet. Opening a result does not scroll to the match.
- OD-011: route changes wait for the pending save to finish. A localStorage draft is always written, and on pagehide a keepalive save is also sent when the body is under 60 KiB. When a note opens, a draft based on the server's current revision is saved. A draft that conflicts with a newer server revision is kept as a version entry, so its content is not lost.
- OD-012: the indicator shows Offline when navigator.onLine is false or the save fails with a network error. Edits are then queued in localStorage and retried when the browser fires the online event. An HTTP error response shows Unable to save, with a retry control next to the indicator.
- OD-013: password reset uses a single-use link sent by email. The token is valid for 60 minutes and stored only as a hash. Completing a reset revokes all of the user's sessions.
- OD-014: the label for untitled notes is the text Untitled note.
- OD-015: Ctrl+Alt+N (Cmd+Option+N on macOS) creates a new note, and the shortcut is ignored while the AltGraph modifier is active. The shortcut is not configurable.
- OD-016: deleting a folder also deletes its subfolders. The user's chosen outcome applies to every non-trashed note, active or archived, anywhere in the deleted subtree.
- OD-017: search matches tag names, and the tag picker filters tags as the user types.
- OD-018: the full export is a ZIP file. Folders become directories, and tags, pinned, and archived state go in YAML front matter. Archived notes are included and trashed notes are excluded.
- OD-019: import accepts .md files, .txt files, and a .zip of them. Directories in the ZIP become folders, and the front matter fields tags and folder are honored. Files in the ZIP that a note links to by relative path become attachments.
- OD-020: only the full-collection export asks for confirmation.
- OD-021: the date-range filter uses a user choice between created and updated, defaulting to updated.
- OD-022: the breakpoint is 768 px. Narrower viewports get the mobile drawer layout.
- OD-023: the contrast standard is WCAG 2.2 AA.
- OD-024: the supported matrix is current stable Chrome and Edge, run through the Playwright channels chrome and msedge, and current Firefox and Safari, represented by Playwright's Firefox and WebKit builds. Each runs at desktop and mobile viewports. A browser that is not installed fails the run rather than being skipped.
- OD-025: backups run daily, the newest 14 are kept, and the restore target is 1 hour.
- OD-026: the note statuses for search are active, archived, trashed, pinned, and open tasks. Without a status filter, search covers active and archived notes.
- OD-027: pasted content keeps headings, bold, italic, lists, links, block quotes, and code. Everything else is reduced to plain text.
- OD-028: these deletion actions ask for confirmation, with these confirm labels: permanent deletion (Delete permanently), folder deletion (Delete folder), tag deletion (Delete tag), and attachment removal (Remove attachment). Moving a note to trash does not ask, because the note can be restored from Trash.
- OD-029: on mobile, an open note's editor fills the viewport.
- OD-030: pinned notes are listed first only under the default sort and the pinned sort. Other sorts order strictly by their own field.
- OD-031: focus returns to the control that opened a dialog, drawer, or panel when it closes.
- OD-032: a version preview shows that version's own content (the first 200 characters).
- OD-033: the dashboard's recent list is the full active unpinned note list ordered by last update, loaded 50 at a time with a Load more button. Quick access offers New note, Search, Pinned, and Open tasks.

## Tasks

Dev dependencies: tsx, typescript, esbuild, playwright, @axe-core/playwright, pdfjs-dist, and selfsigned. Scripts: build:client (esbuild bundle of src/client/main.ts into dist/client), start, pretest (runs build:client), test (node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts), test:browsers (playwright install chromium firefox webkit), backup, and restore.
- src/server/db/schema.sql: every user-owned table uses a TEXT UUID primary key. Create these tables: users (email unique, password_hash), sessions (token_hash, user_id, expires_at), password_resets (token_hash, expires_at, used_at), and preferences (user_id primary key, JSON settings). Also create folders (user_id, parent_id, name, position, timestamps) and notes (user_id, folder_id, original_folder_id, revision, title, body_json, body_text, pinned, archived, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, unarchived_at, trashed_at, restored_at). notes.folder_id and notes.original_folder_id reference folders with ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a folder never deletes a note.
- src/server/db/schema.sql: create the remaining tables: tags (user_id, name, name_key, color), with a unique index on (user_id, name_key); note_tags; checklist_items (id, note_id, user_id, position, text, done); attachments (user_id, note_id, file_name, mime, size, storage_key, uploaded_at); and note_versions (note_id, user_id, title, body_json, body_text, created_at, reason). Add a notes_fts FTS5 table using the trigram tokenizer with sync triggers. Rows that belong to a note use ON DELETE CASCADE from notes, and every user-owned table has a user_id index.

- src/server/app.ts: serve the application only over HTTPS, with the certificate and key from TLS_CERT_PATH and TLS_KEY_PATH. Send HSTS and a Content-Security-Policy that allows scripts only from self, and images from self and blob: for attachment previews. A separate plain-HTTP listener mounts no routes and answers every request with a 308 redirect to HTTPS and an empty body.
- src/server/app.ts: add one error handler, which also catches JSON parse and busboy errors. Unknown API paths return a JSON 404.

The backup runs daily: it uses better-sqlite3 db.backup() into DATA_DIR/backups/<timestamp>, copies the attachments directory, and prunes to the newest 14 backups. Export restoreBackup(backupDir, dataDir) and handle a --restore command-line flag, which the restore script in package.json calls.
- src/server/auth.ts: implement registration and sign-in. Emails are trimmed and lowercased. Passwords are hashed with node:crypto scrypt and a per-user random salt, and the stored form records the parameters. Sign-in compares in constant time. An incorrect password returns 401 without setting a cookie or creating a session row.
- src/server/auth.ts: implement sessions. The token is 32 random bytes, stored only as a sha256 hash, and sent in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie. requireSession returns 401 with no data for API calls and redirects to /signin for page requests. Sign-out deletes the session row and clears the cookie. Mutating requests are checked against the Origin header.
- src/server/auth.ts: implement password reset. Requesting a reset always returns 202. The token is single-use, valid for 60 minutes, stored hashed, and sent through a pluggable mailer interface (a console mailer in development and SMTP from environment variables otherwise). Completing a reset replaces the hash, marks the token used, and revokes all of the user's sessions.

Any GET, PUT, or DELETE on /api/users/:userId/preferences whose userId is not the current user returns 404 and changes nothing. Export ownedOr404(table, id, userId) and a userScoped query helper. Every route uses them, so a missing item and another user's item both return the same 404 and every list query is filtered by user_id.

Before an auto-save is applied, the previous content goes through recordIfMeaningful in versions.ts.
- src/server/routes/notes.ts: implement the list endpoint. The scope parameter is active (default), archived, or any; trashed notes are always excluded.
